19/G.goal: Explain the role, development pipeline, and motion-support requirements of VR software in creating a sensory virtual reality experience.
19/G.achieves: It provides the foundational understanding of the VR software layer needed to design, build, and optimize XR systems in the course case study.

19/O1.goal: Explain how VR software drives VR hardware and mediates user data to produce a sensory virtual reality experience.
19/O1.achieves: It lets the learner locate software functions between VR hardware and user perception before designing or implementing VR components in the course case study.

19/O2.goal: Describe the software pipeline and developer-support abstractions that create and render a virtual environment for VR users.
19/O2.achieves: It gives the learner a foundation for choosing and reasoning about the software components needed to build a VR application in the course case study.

19/O3.goal: Describe the motion and locomotion support VR software must provide, including matched motion, the matched zone, obstacle mismatch, and alternative locomotion approaches.
19/O3.achieves: It helps the learner anticipate cybersickness and usability constraints when designing VR interactions, which informs later user-experience optimization.
